sam: Flagging a perf regression after the selector heuristics landed. Short-stream latency p99 +22% on host path.

ingrid: where in the host stack? tokenizer, parser, or IO?

sam: instrumented traces point to the streaming emitter. Lots of tiny writev calls and memcpy in tokenizer output path.

ben: saw a correlated rise in KV contention earlier today. Could be more frequent small K/V reads when fragments aren't merged.

sam: yup. The new kernel preference disables the 'coalesce_hint' on fastpath kernels; that means we flush smaller chunks immediately.

toni: can you paste the flame or perf summary?

sam: Perf gist: https://perf.company/rum/176800-emitter.svg and brief: syscall-time doubled for short requests; memcpys up ~40%. Key stack: writev -> grpc_send -> emitter::flush -> tokenizer::emit.

ingrid: can we quick-fix by reintroducing a coalesce layer in the emitter?

sam: local experiment shows coalescing 2-4 small frames into one write cuts p99 by ~30% and reduces kvcache evictions by ~15%. Patch I tested:
```
--- a/emitter/stream_emitter.cpp
+++ b/emitter/stream_emitter.cpp
@@ -120,6 +120,13 @@
-  socket.writev(frags);
+  // batch tiny fragments to avoid syscall and grpc layer churn
+  Fragments batched;
+  for (auto &f : frags) {
+    if (f.size() < 200 && batched.size_bytes() < 800) batched.append(f);
+    else { socket.writev(batched); batched.clear(); socket.writev(f); }
+  }
+  if (!batched.empty()) socket.writev(batched);
```

ben: great. Did you run a canary?

sam: canary 10% for 20m: p50 110ms -> 106ms, p95 250ms -> 240ms, p99 470ms -> 330ms. Sys CPU 10% lower. perf-bot posted the numbers.

perf-bot: canary/10%/20m: p50 110ms->106ms, p95 250ms->240ms, p99 470ms->330ms; kvcache.evictions -15%; sys_cpu -10%.

toni: sounds convincing. We should also add a unit-test for the selector to preserve coalesce_hint and a microbench for small-stream latencies so CI catches this.

ci-bot: ticket created RNDF-1222 (selector: preserve coalesce_hint + microbench).

sam: I'm preparing a revert PR for the selector change that removed the hint and a hotfix PR with the emitter coalesce. Planning rollback window tomorrow 09:30 PST if no objections.

b en: small note 4 : some HTTP/1.1 clients show extra header flushes when fragments are tiny; this fix reduces header churn too.

ingrid: please include flamegraphs and the small-stream microbench in the PR. Also add a telemetry gauge for writev calls per request so we can alert on regressions.

sam: will do. pushing PRs now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
